problem: The 40-line threshold is now in two places, root clippy.toml and crates/merge-core/clippy.toml. Clippy reads only the nearest clippy.toml, so changing the root value would silently leave merge-core at the old one (vision 2: one constant per tunable).
fix: Add a one-line CP1 comment to both files citing the clippy configuration docs (the nearest clippy.toml shadows its parents, https://doc.rust-lang.org/clippy/configuration.html) and naming the other file, so a reader changing one copy sees the other.

problem: deny.toml reads `unmaintained = "all"`, but the 'warn, not deny' part of the policy lives only in the justfile's `--warn unmaintained`. Anyone running plain `cargo deny check` gets errors that the gate does not.
fix: Add a one-line CP1 comment here saying that cargo-deny v2 config sets only the scope, and that the severity is lowered to warn by `just deny` with `--warn unmaintained`.

problem: The crate doc line includes a roadmap clause ('and later the Tauri commands'), which goes stale the moment M2 lands and is not part of CP3's single-responsibility line.
fix: Change it to `//! Desktop shell: thin Tauri commands and the IPC types exported to the frontend.`

problem: The generated bindings.ts is in this slice's owned set (.omp/run/slices.json) and ipc-contract says it must be committed, but neither M0S0RustSkeleton.patch nor M0S0WebSkeleton.patch contains it. Applying the patches to a clean tree therefore fails `just bindings-check` (diff: No such file), and so `just check` fails.
fix: Regenerate the patch with frontend/src/ipc/bindings.ts included (output of `just bindings`), so the committed artifact matches what bindings-check diffs against.

problem: RS8 denies unwrap/expect/panic only outside #[cfg(test)], but neither clippy.toml sets the test exemptions. With `--all-targets -D warnings`, the first unit or integration test that uses `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!` fails the gate, which pushes later slices into `#[allow]` (itself a should finding).
fix: Add `allow-unwrap-in-tests = true`, `allow-expect-in-tests = true` and `allow-panic-in-tests = true` to both clippy.toml and crates/merge-core/clippy.toml.

problem: The disallowed-methods list covers only read/read_to_string/read_dir/write/File::open/File::create. The other std::fs write functions (`remove_file`, `remove_dir_all`, `create_dir_all`, `copy`, `rename`) compile clean in merge-core, so PM1's "no std::fs" is only partly enforced.
fix: Add the remaining std::fs mutating functions to disallowed-methods, or add a `grep -rE 'std::(fs|process)' crates/merge-core/src` failure to scripts/arch-check.sh as one exhaustive detector.

problem: Clippy does not merge a crate clippy.toml with the root one, so `too-many-lines-threshold = 40` is duplicated in two files. Editing the root value silently leaves merge-core on the old threshold, which violates vision 2 (one constant per tunable).
fix: Have scripts/arch-check.sh fail when the two files' `too-many-lines-threshold` lines differ, so the duplication is enforced rather than remembered.

problem: `cargo tree` without `--target all --all-features` sees only host-target, default-feature edges. A `cfg(target_os = "macos")` or optional `yamt-merge-core` dep in gitio would pass arch-check on Linux.
fix: Use `cargo tree --package "$1" --edges normal --target all --all-features --prefix none` in normal_deps.

problem: `--no-tests=warn` lets `just test` stay green if a workspace stops compiling any tests (for example a broken filter or a removed tests dir). It is only needed while the skeleton has zero tests.
fix: Drop `--no-tests=warn` in the first slice that adds a Rust test, so the recipe matches §7's `cargo nextest run --workspace`.

problem: Cross-slice issue; the file belongs to M0S0RustSkeleton. The web-* recipes call `pnpm -C frontend vitest run` / `oxlint` / `eslint` directly instead of the package scripts named in brief line 8. As a result `just check` runs the browser project, which cannot launch WebKit on this machine, and fails. It also skips `--max-warnings 0`, so the gate and `pnpm lint` are two definitions that drift.
fix: Change the recipes to `(frontend "lint")`, `(frontend "typecheck")`, `(frontend "test")`, `(frontend "sfc-order")` and `(frontend "fmt:check")`, so frontend/package.json is the one place each web gate is defined.

problem: `types: ["vite/client", "node"]` applies to all of src/. Webview code under src/editor or src/ui can use `process.env` or `Buffer` and still typecheck, then fail at runtime. `setTimeout` is also typed as returning `NodeJS.Timeout` instead of `number`.
fix: Split the config: an app tsconfig for src/** with `types: ["vite/client"]`, and a node tsconfig for scripts/** and vite.config.ts with `types: ["node"]`, both referenced from tsconfig.json (the stock vite vue-ts layout). Point vue-tsc at both, e.g. with `-b`.

problem: The framework-free fence blocks only the exact `vue` specifier. `import { ref } from "@vue/reactivity"`, `@vue/runtime-core` or `vue/…` subpaths in src/editor, src/model or src/connectors pass lint, which breaks PM3 and decision 22.
fix: Add `"vue/*"` and `"@vue/*"` to the PM3 pattern group next to `@vueuse/*` and `@tauri-apps/*`.

problem: The ui override's internal group is `["../editor/internal/*", "**/internal/*"]`. It is missing the bare `**/internal` entry that the base, ipc and editor groups all have, so `import … from "../editor/internal"` (which resolves to internal/index.ts) passes lint from src/ui.
fix: Add `"**/internal"` to the ui override's internal group so all four PM5 groups have the same shape.

problem: `layoutRulesOff` turns off every eslint-plugin-vue rule whose meta.type is "layout". The brief says flat/recommended only, and this change to the Vue ruleset is not in the accepted deviations.
fix: Either remove `layoutRulesOff`, or keep it and report it in deviations_from_brief, naming the oxfmt conflict that motivated it so the orchestrator can record it.

problem: log.ts exports seven names. LogLevel, LogFields, LogForward and Log have no importer anywhere in src/; only createLog, LogEntry (used by the test) and log are consumed.
fix: Drop `export` from LogLevel, LogFields, LogForward and Log; keep LogEntry, createLog and log.

problem: The forward-failure path builds the `[error] … {…}` line by hand, so the line format exists both here and in mirror().
fix: Replace it with `mirror({ level: "error", event: "log.forward_failed", fields: { reason: String(error) } })`.

problem: src/ipc, src/ui and src/editor already contain real files, so their .gitkeep files do nothing. Brief line 6 asked for ipc/.gitkeep only if bindings.ts was absent.
fix: Delete .gitkeep from src/ipc, src/ui and src/editor; keep it only in the still-empty model/, connectors/ and fixtures/.

problem: Statements that are not classified are skipped silently. A composable call such as `const store = useAppStore()` or `useMergeController(...)` (VU9/VU11, the two composables v0 components will call) placed after function declarations or lifecycle hooks passes `pnpm sfc-order`.
fix: In calleeSection, classify any Identifier callee matching `/^use[A-Z]/` as "state", so composables join the ref/useTemplateRef section and their misplacement is reported.

problem: VU2 orders all "lifecycle hooks" and watch effects, but CALLEE_SECTIONS lists only six hooks and two watchers. A misplaced onActivated, onDeactivated, onErrorCaptured, onRenderTracked, onRenderTriggered, onServerPrefetch, watchPostEffect, watchSyncEffect or shallowReactive after a function declaration is not reported.
fix: Add the missing Vue lifecycle hooks to "lifecycle", watchPostEffect and watchSyncEffect to "watch", and shallowReactive to "state".

problem: LogForward is typed `(entry) => void`, so an async forward (the planned forward is `commands.log`, which returns a Promise) type-checks. Its rejection then escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, skips the `log.forward_failed` path, and breaks the 'never throws' guarantee for the only real forward.
fix: Type LogForward as `(entry: LogEntry) => Promise<unknown> | void`. When forward returns a Promise, attach `.catch((error) => mirror({ level: "error", event: "log.forward_failed", ... }))`, and keep the try/catch for synchronous throws.

problem: The throwing-forward test mocks console.error but never asserts on it. Emptying the catch body at log.ts:52, which is the exact path rework item 3 changed, would leave the suite green.
fix: Assert that console.error was called with '[error] apply.chunk {id: 1}' and then '[error] log.forward_failed {reason: "Error: ipc down"}'.

problem: No test covers the IPC8 debug gate. Deleting `level === "debug" && !import.meta.env.DEV`, or dropping the `!`, keeps both tests passing, even though production would then forward debug entries over IPC (or dev would lose them).
fix: Add a log.test.ts case that uses `vi.stubEnv("DEV", false)` to show `log.debug` mirrors but does not forward, and `vi.stubEnv("DEV", true)` to show it forwards once, with `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` in afterEach.

problem: The ui→model group matches only `../model` and `../model/*`. A component in a ui subdirectory importing `../../model/x` passes lint, while the bindings and internal groups use the depth-independent `**/` form.
fix: Change the group to `["**/model", "**/model/**"]`, matching the shape of the `**/ipc/bindings` and `**/internal` groups.

problem: The script that gates `just check` has no automated test, only the manual one-off proof from acceptance. A regression that makes classify return undefined for every statement (for example a compiler-sfc or typescript API change) turns the gate into a silent pass on every file.
fix: Have firstViolation take `(file, text)`, export it, and add `scripts/check-sfc-order.test.ts` to the node Vitest project. Cover one in-order SFC, one with function-before-computed (asserting the reported line), and one with a composable after a lifecycle hook.

problem: `String(error)` itself throws a TypeError when forward throws a value with no toString (for example `Object.create(null)`), so that error escapes `emit` despite the never-throw contract.
fix: Use `error instanceof Error ? error.message : typeof error` for `reason`.

problem: Orchestrator asked the verifier to tamper a file as a smoke step; the verifier is read-only by design and the ownership hook blocked it
fix: Smoke recipes that mutate files belong to the implementer's acceptance; verifier recipes are read-only commands only (clarify in skill://verification and skill://orchestrate)

problem: Session 2 was started in frontend/ instead of the repo root; project settings (.omp/config.yml modelRoles implementer/reviewer/verifier) are loaded only from the process cwd, so every project agent failed at spawn with a misleading 'No model selected' error (5 spawns, <1s each). Proven: `omp --model=@implementer -p` works from repo root, 'Model "@implementer" not found' from frontend/

problem: The only thing that drops every acyclic file's singleton SCC is the `edge === undefined` early return. It reads like a defensive guard, so a reader has to reverse-engineer Tarjan output to learn that 'first member has no edge into its component' means 'not a cycle'.

problem: The `?raw` test imports `./theme.css?raw`, which matches no rule and no known file with or without stripping. It still passes if QUERY_SUFFIX stripping (fences.ts:21,150) is deleted, so query stripping has no test that fails without it.
fix: Keep the brief's non-violating shape but make stripping matter: add a second case, e.g. a ui file importing `../model?raw`, expecting PM2 (it is missed without stripping because `src/model?raw` is not inside `src/model`), or assert that a `?raw` import of a known file creates the expected edge.

problem: FRAMEWORK_FREE_MODULES is a membership set written as `Record<string, true>` + `Object.hasOwn`, while the same file uses `ReadonlySet<string>` for the same kind of check at line 141.
fix: Declare `const FRAMEWORK_FREE_MODULES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["editor", "model", "connectors"])` and test it with `.has(module)`.

problem: Any resolved path with an `internal` segment outside src/ is reported as PM5. Probed: src/ui/sample.ts importing `../../fixtures/internal/a.txt?raw` gives a PM5 violation, even though under the brief a module is only a first directory under src/.
fix: Bind `const targetModule = MODULE_OF.exec(target)?.[1]` and report PM5 only when `targetModule !== undefined && targetModule !== module && target.split("/").includes("internal")`. Then add a test showing that a ui `?raw` import from `../../fixtures/internal/x.txt` is allowed.

problem: The `?raw` test still passes if QUERY_SUFFIX stripping is deleted: `src/editor/theme.css?raw` violates nothing with or without the query, so nothing proves 'query suffixes are stripped before resolving'.
fix: Add an assertion where the query would hide a violation, e.g. `src/ui/s.ts` with `import "../model?raw"` expecting one PM2 on `src/ui/s.ts`. Keep the existing no-violation case.

problem: The whole suite still passes if `.ts` or `.vue` is removed from RESOLVE_SUFFIXES (fences.ts:23). The only cycle fixture uses `./b`→`b/index.ts` and an explicit `../a.ts`, so the most common form, an extensionless sibling `./b`→`b.ts`, could stop producing cycle edges without any test failing.
fix: Make the cycle fixture `src/model/a.ts` (`import "./b"`) ↔ `src/model/b.ts` (`import "./a"`), or add that as a second case, plus one cycle edge that resolves through `.vue` (e.g. `src/ui/A.vue` ↔ `src/ui/b.ts` via `./A`). Expect exactly one PM5 per cycle.

problem: `text-white` here and in FileList.vue:21 takes its colour from Tailwind's default theme (`--color-white`), not from the yamt palette. Because style.css never resets the defaults, every stock Tailwind colour (`red-500`, `zinc-*`, …) is still available as a second palette next to `@theme`.
fix: Add `--color-*: initial;` at the top of the `@theme static` block and a `--color-on-primary` token. Then use `text-on-primary` in both places, so the `@theme` block is the only source of colours.

problem: Looking up a language needs `Object.hasOwn` plus a ternary (pane.ts:96-99), and the result goes into a local named `language` that holds a factory, not a language name.
fix: Make `LANGUAGES` a `ReadonlyMap<string, () => Extension>` and inline `(pane.language === null ? undefined : LANGUAGES.get(pane.language))?.() ?? []`. Alternatively, rename the local to `languageExtension`.

problem: `PaneKind` is exported, but nothing outside pane.ts uses it: index.ts passes string literals.
fix: Remove `export` from `type PaneKind` until a second module needs it.

problem: The 'scroll each .cm-scroller to the bottom, then read the last gutter line' probe cannot tell whether a pane scrolls on its own. CodeMirror renders a 1000px margin beyond the visible area, so all 81 lines (about 1475px) are in the DOM at scrollTop 0 and lastGutterLine would be [81,76,76] even if a scroller never moved. Independent per-pane scrolling therefore rests only on the screenshot.
fix: Extend the DOM-facts probe to record each scroller's scrollHeight > clientHeight and its scrollTop after the scroll (expect > 0), and paste that into the evidence.

problem: Only 3 unchanged lines separate the remote-only subtotal change from the discount conflict, and the conflict from the remote-only tax change. At gap ≥ 3 (the 'loose grouping' the architecture open question considers) both remote-only chunks would be absorbed into the conflict, and the sample would lose its 'remote changes a different function' shape.
fix: Move one unchanged function (e.g. summary or createCart) between subtotal and discount, and another between discount and tax, so the four shapes stay separate for any plausible gap.

problem: Respawning an implementer under its finished name (isolated agents cannot be revived) got the task name suffixed `-2`, which slices.json did not list, so the ownership hook had no entry for the live agents until the orchestrator rewrote the registry after spawning; the registry hook also rejects keeping the finished names because their globs overlap
fix: Rework spawns use an explicit new name (e.g. `M1WindowShellR1`) and slices.json is rewritten with only the live names before spawning; proposal for retro: one line in orchestrate step 6

problem: A broadcast to all agents (to tell the two live implementers to retry) also woke four idle reviewers, briefly running six agents against the cap of two; they were stopped within seconds and did nothing
fix: Message live agents by name, never broadcast while idle agents exist

problem: Isolated agents run in a copy of the last commit, and the ownership hook reads .omp/run/slices.json from that copy (resolve(cwd, ...)); a registry change that is written but not committed before spawning is invisible to the agents, so both rework agents were blocked on every edit and one aborted (about 2 minutes lost)
fix: Orchestrate step 3: write slices.json AND commit it before spawning isolated agents; proposal for retro: the slice-registry or task-fanout hook warns when slices.json differs from HEAD at spawn time

problem: The deadline only covers git's own exit: stdout/stderr are joined afterwards with no time limit. `checkout -m -- <path>` runs the user's post-checkout hook, whose stdout goes to stderr; if that hook starts a background process that keeps stderr open, checkout_merge blocks indefinitely despite GIT_TIMEOUT.
fix: Have the reader threads send their results over an `mpsc` channel and receive with `recv_timeout(deadline - now)`, returning `Error::Timeout` when the shared deadline passes.

problem: No test covers the brief's rule that a non-`blob` type returns UnexpectedOutput and leaves the reader usable. If a regression returned before `read_content_and_newline`, the cat-file stream would fall out of sync and every later `read` would fail, and no test would notice.
fix: Extend test 5: read the HEAD commit oid (fixture `git rev-parse HEAD` → `Oid::parse`), assert `UnexpectedOutput { command: "cat-file", .. }`, then assert the next `read(&entries[0].oid)` still returns BASE.

problem: find_git_on_path accepts relative PATH entries: an empty entry gives `git`, which is looked up on PATH again, and `bin` gives `bin/git`. Command then resolves these against current_dir(root) (std documents this as platform-specific), not the directory where git was found, so the binary that runs may not be the one 'resolved once' in discover.
fix: Skip entries where `!dir.is_absolute()` in the PATH loop so Repo.git is always an absolute path.

problem: The once-per-path removal record is hidden inside the per-stage loop as `enumerate()` + `if index == 0`, so a reader has to infer the 'first record of each path' structure from an index check (principles §2, vision 1).
fix: Make the dedupe loop keep the first entry of each path (`firsts: Vec<&StageEntry>`), then write `for first in firsts { push_removal_record(&mut input, first); for entry in entries.iter().filter(|e| e.path == first.path) { push_stage_record(&mut input, entry); } }`.

problem: The stdin writer thread is created with `child.stdin.take().zip(stdin).map(|(mut pipe, bytes)| thread::spawn(..))`. Option::zip is an obscure combinator for a Rust-beginner reader, and it hides the plain rule 'spawn a writer only when there is input' (vision 1, principles §2).
fix: Use `let writer = if let (Some(mut pipe), Some(bytes)) = (child.stdin.take(), stdin) { Some(thread::spawn(move || pipe.write_all(&bytes))) } else { None };`.

problem: Doc comments on non-merge-core items restate names or fields, which is outside CP2 (merge-core public items only): blob.rs:9 (BlobReader), repo.rs:14 (Repo), entry.rs:10 (Oid: SHA1_HEX_LEN and SHA256_HEX_LEN already say it), entry.rs:36 (Stage numbering, repeated by index_number), entry.rs:63 (StageEntry), entry.rs:111 (index_info), run.rs:12 (Access: the match says it), run.rs:43 (run). run.rs:108 explains what `None` means instead of the type saying it. entry.rs:75 is a git-format fact without a reference.
fix: Delete the restating doc comments. Return a named enum `Waited { Exited(ExitStatus), TimedOut }` from wait_or_kill in place of the run.rs:108 comment. Keep entry.rs:75 as a CP1 `//` line citing git-ls-files(1) `-z` output.

problem: The test-11 reap check reads /proc/self/task/*/children with unwrap, so `cargo nextest run -p yamt-gitio` panics on macOS, which the brief names as a target platform (plan: 'Also runs on: macOS (arm64)').
fix: Mark child_pids_of_this_process and its final assert_eq with `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, so the Timeout and elapsed-time assertions still run on macOS.

problem: The GitFailed Display shows the status as Debug (`exit status Some(128)`) and appends git's raw stderr, including its trailing newline, so the user-facing message ends in `\n` and shows Rust Option syntax.
fix: Store `stderr.trim_end()` in run.rs:67 and render the status with `status.map_or_else(|| "killed by signal".to_owned(), |code| format!("exit status {code}"))` in the #[error] arguments.

problem: Each git subcommand name is written twice: as the error label (`LS_FILES` here, `CAT_FILE` in blob.rs:7, `"rev-parse"` in repo.rs:27) and again as a separate literal in the argv in repo.rs:23/41/46, so the two can drift apart (vision 2).
fix: Use the same const in both places, e.g. `self.command(Access::Read, &[LS_FILES, "-u", "-z"])` with the const made pub(crate), or move the error label next to the argv in repo.rs.

problem: `triple()` has no path that gives both sides the same edit. [INFERENCE] So BothSame chunks in proptests 3 and 7 come almost only from both sides happening to set the same new last line, a few percent of cases and nearly always at EOF. A BothSame classification bug for mid-file regions, or for regions merged through the gap, would rarely be generated.
fix: Add a `shared` arm to `triple()` that applies one common edit list to base, then separate extra edit lists per side. Also run proptests 3 and 7 on `(base, local, local)`, where every two-sided region must be BothSame.

problem: Proptest 4 checks `.iter().all(..)` over the chunk list. It would still pass if `compute_chunks` returned no chunks at all, so on its own it does not show that the changed side's edits are reported.
fix: In each leg, also assert `chunks.is_empty() == (changed_side == base)`, e.g. `prop_assert_eq!(kinds(base, base, remote).is_empty(), remote == base)`.

problem: The heart of architecture step 4 is called `SideDiff::map` (called as `local.map(&region.base)`, line 94). A TS-proficient reader takes that for Array.map. Its helper `side_line(preceding_hunks: usize, ..)` receives a partition count, so the reader has to work out the `<` (start) vs `<=` (end) asymmetry from names alone.
fix: Rename `map` to `map_base_to_side`, the name architecture §3.1 step 4 uses. Rename `starting_within` to `starting_at_or_before_end` so the `<=` boundary rule (an insertion at the region end belongs to the region) is in the name.

problem: Each match arm (lines 16, 19, 21) rebuilds a `Range<u32>` from a typed `LineRange` with `x.start.0..x.end().0`. The tail at line 28 slices base lines a second way (`.get(next as usize..)`), so one function uses two slicing idioms.
fix: Use `lines_in` for the tail too (`lines_in(&base_lines, &(next_base_line..len))`). Or have a private helper take `(start, len)` so the arms read `lines_in(&local_lines, chunk.local.start.0, chunk.local.len)`.

problem: `Options` and `DEFAULT_GAP` are inputs to `compute_chunks` but live in `chunk.rs`, the module for output types. A reader looking for what `gap` controls opens the wrong file first.
fix: Move `Options`, its `Default` impl and `DEFAULT_GAP` into `compute.rs` next to `compute_chunks`, their only consumer, and re-export them from there in lib.rs.

problem: `closed_pipe()` is now defined twice with identical bodies, here and in blob.rs:78, because the rework copied it from blob.rs instead of sharing it (vision 2).
fix: Make run.rs's `closed_pipe` `pub(crate)`, import it in blob.rs next to `argv` (`use crate::run::{argv, closed_pipe};`), and delete the copy in blob.rs.

problem: The nested generic `Receiver<io::Result<Vec<u8>>>` is spelled out three times (run.rs:117, 131, 132), which a Rust-beginner reader has to re-parse at each signature (vision 1).
fix: Add `type PipeOutput = Receiver<io::Result<Vec<u8>>>;` next to `Waited` and use it in read_on_thread and receive_output.

problem: [0.1] The invariant 'every chunk of (base, local, local) is BothSame' is asserted twice, at lines 224 and 280. Neither test name describes it, while proptest 4's local==remote leg (line 249) asserts the weaker `!contains(Conflict)`. This breaks the original brief's 'each invariant is its own named test'.
fix: Replace line 249 with `prop_assert!(both_changed.iter().all(|kind| *kind == ChunkKind::BothSame))` and delete lines 224 and 280. Proptests 3 and 7 then keep only the `for triple in [triple, shared]` loop.

problem: [0.1] The one saved seed (`base: "", local: "x", remote: ""`) came from the reverted item-3 mutation (`compute_chunks` returning `Vec::new()`), not from a failure of real code. The new file records debris from a throwaway run.
fix: Delete the untracked file before committing. Let proptest recreate it only when real code fails.

problem: git add keeps a resolve-undo record and `git checkout -m` rebuilds the conflict from it, so a finish-then-reset test passes even when session captures stages lazily; the RK1 proving test as registered cannot catch the bug it exists for (found by the 0.2 implementer).
fix: RK1 test row: clear the resolve-undo record (`git update-index --clear-resolve-undo`) after finish before asserting reset restores the captured stages.

problem: No risk row for non-regular files: a submodule conflict (mode 160000) made `MergeSession::open` fail for the whole merge, and a symlink conflict (mode 120000) would be decoded as text and written back as a regular file.
fix: Add a risk row (owner session: mode-based unsupported reason; test: open on a merge with a submodule/symlink conflict lists it as unsupported and the other files stay usable).

problem: If `restore_stages` succeeds and `checkout_merge` then fails (timeout, git error), the index is unmerged again but the status stays Resolved, so files() shows Resolved and remaining() undercounts compared with `ls-files -u`.
fix: Set the status to Unresolved right after `restore_stages` returns Ok, before calling `checkout_merge`.

problem: Decoding stops at the first side that fails and runs Binary → TooLarge → NonUtf8 per side, so a Latin-1 base with a NUL-containing local is reported NonUtf8 rather than Binary as the brief's "any side with a NUL → Binary" rule says. Every fixture fails identically on all three sides, so no test pins the cross-side order.
fix: Run each check across all three sides in the brief's order (NUL probe on every side, then UTF-8, then size, or state the chosen order in the brief), and add a decode unit test whose sides fail differently, e.g. a non-UTF-8 base with a binary local.

problem: The "local when base is empty" EOL branch is never exercised: no test loads an add/add file with CRLF, so replacing `eol_source` with `&texts.base` keeps every test green, and an add/add CRLF file would then report Lf (RK5).
fix: Give the ADD_ADD fixture CRLF line breaks, or add a test that loads a CRLF add/add file and asserts `eol == Eol::CrLf`.

problem: Reset is only proven after finish on a modify/modify file. An add/add file (no base stage in the replayed index-info) and a reset of a file that was never finished (which the brief says must work) have no test, so a regression in either path goes unnoticed.
fix: Parameterise the reset test over a modify/modify and an add/add ConflictFile, and add a case that resets without finishing first; each asserts `ls-files -u` is identical and the worktree contains `<<<<<<<`.

problem: The TooLarge fixture is 8 MiB + 1 byte, so changing `>` to `>=` in decode_side still passes; the size boundary is not pinned the way the NUL window is.
fix: In decode.rs tests, assert that `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` bytes decode Ok and `MAX_TEXT_BYTES + 1` bytes give TooLarge.

problem: hash_object ignores the child's exit status and silently skips the write when stdin is missing, so a failing `git hash-object` yields Ok("") instead of an error.
fix: Check `output.status.success()` and return `Error::GitFailed` with the stderr, as git_ok does.

problem: finish (line 126) and reset (line 139) each look the path up twice: first with file(), then with file_mut() at the end. The second lookup's UnknownPath branch can never fire, but a reader still has to work out why it cannot fail.
fix: Replace the file()/file_mut() pair with one free fn `find_file(files: &mut [FileState], path: &str) -> Result<&mut FileState>`. Call it once per method as `let file = find_file(&mut self.files, path)?;` and set `file.status` directly; the disjoint borrows of `self.files` and `self.repo` compile.

problem: The lookup calls display_path(), which allocates a new String for every file it compares on each load/finish/reset, but only to test equality.
fix: In the lookup, compare without allocating: `file.path.to_string_lossy() == path` (Cow<str> == &str). Keep display_path() only for building the DTOs.

problem: The comment states an external git fact (checkout -m refuses delete/modify paths) but gives no source, so a reader cannot check it or tell which git version it applies to.
fix: Add the source on the same line, e.g. `(git builtin/checkout.c checkout_merged; observed on git 2.56)`.

problem: hash_object never checks the exit status and silently skips writing when stdin is missing, so a failed `git hash-object` returns Ok("") or the hash of empty input instead of an Err. That is a fake fallback in a library whose contract is to return Result.
fix: Turn a missing stdin into an error with `child.stdin.take().ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other("hash-object stdin not piped"))?`, and return Error::GitFailed when `!output.status.success()`, as git_ok does.

problem: `handle(chunk, status, side, value)` is a vague verb with four positional parameters, so a reader of `statusAfterApply` has to open it to learn that it sets every changed side of a non-conflict and only the clicked side of a conflict.

problem: iconElement runs the HTML fragment parser (`innerHTML`) twice for every visible arrow row on every requestAnimationFrame, and scrolling triggers one per frame (scrollSync → #requestFrame → paintStrips), so the same five constant SVG strings are re-parsed dozens of times per scroll frame.

problem: The CM8 test deletes only a fully open conflict; deleting a half-handled conflict (one side applied or ignored) is the new combination this slice creates, and a regression that made collapsedByUser fire only while both sides are pending would pass every test.

problem: Skipping blank and whitespace-only lines (indent.ts:10) is not pinned: none of the fixtures has a blank line inside a block. problem: `\r?` in the split has no observable effect, because a trailing `\r` never changes the leading whitespace and `trim()` already treats `\r` as blank. The CRLF input in indent.test.ts:69 therefore proves nothing, although the report says it does.

problem: Any yamt that is not an AppImage (.deb, source build) started from a process that was itself launched from some other AppImage (e.g. the terminal of an AppImage-packaged editor) inherits that AppImage's APPIMAGE and OWD. It then resolves `.`/a relative --repo against the other program's start directory instead of the real cwd, and fails with 'not a git repository' (exit 2) or opens the wrong repository.
fix: Use OWD only when the running binary lives inside the mounted AppImage: in repo_from_start_dir, check that `std::env::current_exe()` starts with `$APPDIR`. Pass that check (or the exe path and APPDIR) into `resolved`, and add a test where APPIMAGE/OWD are set but the exe is outside APPDIR, so the repo stays.

problem: The Use section and the alias (`git config --global alias.resolve '!yamt'`) need a `yamt` command on PATH, but only the .deb provides one. The AppImage stays `yamt_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage` wherever it was downloaded, and on macOS the binary is `/Applications/yamt.app/Contents/MacOS/yamt`; a Finder start runs with cwd `/` and exits 2 with its message on an invisible stderr. Following the README on macOS or with the AppImage gives 'command not found' (sharpens #354).
fix: In Install, add the PATH step per format: AppImage `install -m755 yamt_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage ~/.local/bin/yamt`; macOS `sudo ln -s /Applications/yamt.app/Contents/MacOS/yamt /usr/local/bin/yamt`. Add one sentence that yamt is started from a terminal in the repository, not by double-clicking.

problem: The release artifacts (AppImage, .deb, .dmg) carry neither LICENSE nor THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, and the notices file gives licence counts instead of the copyright and licence texts that MIT/BSD/ISC/Apache-2.0 require for binary redistribution. 'Each crate's license text ships in its source package' does not reach someone who only downloads a binary, and the LGPL GTK/WebKitGTK copies in the AppImage get only a pointer to the upstream sites, without the Ubuntu 22.04 versions.
fix: Generate a full-text notices file (copyright lines plus licence texts per crate/package; a generator like cargo-about needs a plan row per DR3, otherwise concatenate the LICENSE files from `cargo metadata`/node_modules in a script). Ship it with LICENSE through `bundle.resources` in tauri.conf.json, and name the exact Ubuntu 22.04 source package versions of the bundled LGPL libraries.

problem: `is_page_gone(&mut self, …)` reads like a query but drains the answer channel and overwrites `unanswered_since`, so calling it twice changes the answer. fix: Split it: a pure `fn page_gone(unanswered_since: Option<Instant>, request_at: Instant) -> bool` that the tests call directly, and a `record_close_request(&mut self, at)` that drains `answers`, calls page_gone, and stores `at`.

problem: CI pins pnpm 12.0.0 while nothing in the repo records the pnpm version that wrote frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml (no `packageManager` field, no doc). `--frozen-lockfile` can therefore fail on the first tag run if CI's pnpm writes a different lockfile format.

problem: The code decides it is inside an AppImage only from the inherited variables APPIMAGE and OWD. A deb-installed or source-built yamt started from any process that leaked them resolves the default `.` against the parent's OWD. Examples: a shell under another AppImage, or the terminal of an AppImage-packaged editor such as Cursor ([INFERENCE] that Cursor leaks them). The result is the wrong repository or exit 2. This is a regression, because before the patch the default `.` was taken from the current directory.
fix: Treat the process as inside an AppImage only when `std::env::current_exe()` starts with `$APPDIR`. Have `repo_from_start_dir` compute that bool and pass it to `resolved`. Add a test where APPIMAGE and OWD are set but the binary is outside APPDIR and the repo stays `.`.

problem: "run `yamt` in the repository" and the `!yamt` git alias work only for the .deb, which installs /usr/bin/yamt. The AppImage ("make it executable, then run it") and the macOS .app never put `yamt` on PATH, so the user gets `command not found`. Starting the app from the file manager or Finder (the README's own first-run step for macOS) runs it outside a repository: it exits 2 with no window and only an unseen stderr line.
fix: Add one PATH line per install: AppImage `install -m755 yamt_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage ~/.local/bin/yamt`; macOS `sudo ln -s /Applications/yamt.app/Contents/MacOS/yamt /usr/local/bin/yamt` after the first right-click → Open. Add one sentence that yamt starts from a terminal in a repository, so double-clicking it shows nothing.

problem: The `!result.is_empty()` check is the only thing separating a dead page from a live one, and no test covers it (#353); a cargo-mutants deletion of `!` survives. The macOS gap is therefore not a missing callback but this unpinned string contract.

problem: There is no minimum age for "unanswered": a second close request 100 ms after the first destroys the window if the ping has not come back yet. A double-click on × while the page's JS is busy (e.g. right after opening a large file) therefore closes a live page without its 'Cancel File Merge' question and loses unsaved work ([INFERENCE] on timing).
fix: Treat the page as gone only when the earlier request has been unanswered for at least a named `UNANSWERED_CLOSE_GRACE` (e.g. 1 s) and at most UNANSWERED_CLOSE_TIMEOUT. While it is younger than the grace, keep `since` instead of replacing it. Add boundary tests at the grace and at grace − 1 ms.

problem: If OWD is set but empty, `PathBuf::from("").join(".")` stays relative and resolves against $APPDIR/usr. The user then gets a puzzling 'not a git repository' about a path they never gave, and no test covers this case.
fix: Use OWD only when it is a non-empty absolute path (`start.is_absolute()`), and add a test for `Some("")`.

problem: Nothing regenerates or compares THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt, though it is marked GENERATED: the release ships whatever copy is committed, and the justfile line 'run after a dependency change' is the only guard (the implementer's own open_risk). Its `sort -u` also depends on the locale (bit-set sorts after bitflags here), so a regeneration under C.UTF-8 on CI or on another machine would reorder the whole file.
fix: Add `export LC_ALL=C` at the top of scripts/third-party-licenses.sh and regenerate once. Then add a release step on both runners, before `ubuntu-versions`, that runs `scripts/third-party-licenses.sh && git diff --exit-code THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt`, so a stale committed file fails the release instead of shipping.

LGPLv3 §4(b) requires the combined work to carry 'a copy of the GNU GPL and this license document', so the shipped licence file is still incomplete for those libraries.

problem: `record_close_request` returns the page-gone bool, but its name says only that it records. The call site `if self.record_close_request(Instant::now())` (window.rs:84) therefore reads as 'if the request was recorded, destroy the window'. The implementer flagged this in open_risks.

problem: The grace boundary is written twice: `< UNANSWERED_CLOSE_GRACE` here and `UNANSWERED_CLOSE_GRACE..=` in `page_gone` (window.rs:114). The two must stay complementary by hand.
fix: Compute `let unanswered_for = self.unanswered_since.map(|since| at.duration_since(since));` once, and derive both `gone` and 'keep since' from that one value (or have `page_gone` take the `Option<Duration>`).

problem: `current_exe()` on Linux is the kernel-resolved /proc/self/exe path, but the runtime builds APPDIR from `$TMPDIR/.mount_*` without resolving it. With a TMPDIR that is relative or goes through a symlink, a real AppImage counts as outside, and `yamt` run in a repository resolves `.` against `$APPDIR/usr` and exits 2 (the round-1 bug comes back for those users).

problem: Both PATH lines fail on a clean machine: `install -m755 … ~/.local/bin/yamt` errors when ~/.local/bin does not exist, and on fresh Apple Silicon macOS /usr/local/bin is absent, so `sudo ln -s … /usr/local/bin/yamt` (line 20) errors with 'No such file or directory' [INFERENCE: known VS Code `code` shim issue].

problem: An open find bar (find.ts:131, `top = true`) shrinks and pushes down only that pane's scroller. problem: ctrlKey is accepted on macOS, where Ctrl+click is the system secondary click: its mousedown (button 0, ctrlKey) applies the change and WebKit then opens the context menu. problem: For a file deleted locally whose base is empty or absent (an empty base file, or an add by them with no stage 1), eol_source falls to the deleted local text, which is "". The file is then reported as Lf even when the kept remote is CRLF. The editor then sets no lineSeparator and sliceDoc writes the result with LF. The mirrored remote-deleted case detects CrLf from local.

problem: The expected short_id comes from conflict-repo's isolated git (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null), but the session's `log --format=%h` runs through gitio::git_command, which reads the user's config. On a machine with `core.abbrev` set globally, every Commit assertion fails. The same applies to crates/gitio/tests/merge_heads.rs:140.

problem: %(refname:short) prints 'heads/<name>' when a tag of the same name exists (verified with a probe). With one branch the header then shows 'heads/remote', and with several branches the MERGE_MSG name 'remote' no longer matches, so the result falls back to Commit.

problem: chmod 000 on MERGE_MSG does not stop root from reading it, so as root the merge message names 'remote' and the test fails because it gets Branch instead of None.

problem: The 'still active' guard misses a pending user open. Click Mark resolved, then click a not-yet-opened file B before the finish returns: `active` is still the finished file, so moveOn opens the next unresolved file C, and its newer `latestLoad` ticket throws away B's load. The window shows C, not the file the user clicked.

problem: 'a finish of a file no longer shown does not switch files' still passes with the active guard deleted: the next unresolved file after a.ts is b.ts, which is already active, so open(b.ts) does nothing anyway.

A rebuild sets summary null and then non-null inside one watcher callback, so the watch never sees a change: a rebuilt controller with the kept side still taken would show base while the buttons and the mark say Kept (unreachable today; this is the implementer's open risk).

Accepted cost: settled changes in such a file can no longer be reviewed one by one; yamt re-runs git's merge at start to know what git wrote.

problem: One conflicted path that cannot be read (EACCES, or a submodule whose `rev-parse` fails with a real git error) now makes `MergeSession::open` fail, so yamt does not start, although `refresh` treats the same read error as a warning and skips the file.

problem: If the read-back after a successful `git add` (and likewise in take/reset) fails, finish returns `Err(ReadFailed)` although the file is written and staged. The window then reports a failed write, and because `seen` keeps the pre-write bytes, the next refresh reports yamt's own write as an outside 'changed on disk' change.

problem: `Error::ReadFailed` becomes `IpcError::WriteFailed` with only the io message, so problemText.ts will show 'writing <path> failed: Permission denied' when yamt failed to read the file before any write.

problem: Files yamt deliberately never stages (a working-tree-encoding file, a submodule that is no longer checked out) are reported as `MarkersLeft { conflicts: 0 }`. That says 'markers left: none' while meaning 'left alone', and for a UTF-16 file the count comes from parsing UTF-16 bytes, which is meaningless.

problem: To settle one file, changed_on_disk builds a `Vec<Option<OnDisk>>` as long as all files, using a `disk.take()` closure, because `settle` couples its input to file order by position (its doc comment has to explain 'one per file, in file order').

problem: `Located { local: Range<u32>, remote: Range<u32> }` and `Maps::base` carry local and remote lines as bare u32. Passing `located.remote` through `local_to_base` would compile, although vision 4 makes mixing line spaces a type error.

problem: `Seen` is both the last read and the selector for the window's view, so its doc comment has to explain the double meaning, and `load` chooses the view by matching on a field named `seen`.

When a pushed base line does not end in `\n` and is not the last line of the middle, append the disk's line ending (CRLF or LF per `self.eol`). Add a seed test with a base lacking its final newline and a settled line after the block, asserting the middle text and applying ours.

problem: An unspecified `merge` attribute is always treated as the text driver, but git uses `merge.default` for such paths (merge-ll.c `find_ll_merge_driver`). With `merge.default=binary`, git leaves every conflicted text file as ours without markers, yamt's merge-file output has markers, the file counts as changed, and the first `list_files` stages every untouched conflict as ours. The design notes (line 175) list only smudge filters as start false positives that stage.
fix: Resolve the driver as git does: for an unspecified attribute, read `merge.default` (one `git config --get` in gitio) and map `binary`/`union`/`text`/other the same way as an attribute value. Add a start_from_disk case with `merge.default=binary` asserting no disk change.

problem: `merge=<name>` with no `merge.<name>.driver` configured falls back to git's text merge (merge-ll.c: 'default to the 3-way'), but start.rs:107 calls it Custom/changed. A common case is `merge=lfs` written by `git lfs track`, which does not define a driver. Such untouched files open from disk with a MarkersLeft notice. This test pins that false positive: in its hermetic repo git did a plain text merge, because mergiraf is not configured.
fix: Count a name as Custom only when `merge.<name>.driver` is configured (fall back to Text otherwise). Have the test configure `merge.mergiraf.driver` (e.g. a script that writes markers and exits 1), and add an unconfigured-name case expecting no change.

problem: Two blocks can sit inside one local→base hunk: git's zealous refine splits a conflict on ≥4 shared alnum lines both sides added. Both blocks then get the same covering base range, `push_base_lines` writes those base lines twice into the middle, and the chunks overlap in base space. That breaks the invariant that chunks are pairwise disjoint in base space (architecture §3.1). Open risk #3 names wider spans, not duplication.
fix: Clamp each chunk's base range so it starts no earlier than the previous chunk's base end (and push only the clamped lines). Add a seed test with a conflict that git splits into two blocks around 4 shared lines, asserting disjoint base ranges and applying ours on both.

problem: `read_on_disk(...)?` in `open_file` makes one unreadable conflicted path fail the whole open (the app refuses to start; before the patch it opened). Examples: permission denied, or a submodule whose `.git` file points at a missing gitdir. `refresh` skips such a file with a warn.

problem: No test has inputs where histogram and myers merges differ: this test sets `histogram: true` but only checks union output, and every start_from_disk case merges the same either way. Dropping `--diff-algorithm=histogram` or mutating `version >= HISTOGRAM_SINCE` therefore survives (the implementer reports the surviving mutant).

problem: In a_section_line_repeated_elsewhere_still_applies_the_exact_text, the ours view equals local line for line, so the diff has no hunks and the repeated `dup` can never be aligned elsewhere. The test passes for any mapping that is the identity.

problem: `finish` writes with `fs::write`, which follows a symlink. After a text file was replaced by a link and settled (`Seen::Disk(Link)`, view DiskNotText{Link}), a finish with the current version writes the user's text into the link's target, a file yamt never showed (it may be outside the repo).

problem: The scratch dir that holds the base/local/remote blobs is created with the default mode (0777 minus umask, usually 0755), so other local users can read the merge inputs while open runs.

problem: Settlement mixes actions (Add, Remove, LeaveAsIs) with a result name (MarkersLeft), and LeaveAsIs/LeftAsIs differ from DiskResult by one word while MarkersLeft matches it exactly.

problem: `Repo::merge_config` and `attributes` read the developer's global config, but the conflict repos were merged without it. So `cargo test` fails on a machine whose ~/.gitconfig sets `merge.default=binary` (45 failures, among them every disk_is_truth test, e.g. `an_unchanged_disk_reports_nothing…` gets `MarkersLeft{2}`) or has mergiraf's recommended global driver plus attributes (45). A global `merge.<name>.driver` alone breaks `no_config == MergeConfig::default()`.
fix: Run the gitio/session test binaries with the user and system config isolated, e.g. export `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<empty dir>` in `just test` (and document it for bare `cargo test`). In the gitio test, assert only what the repo-local keys add (`config.default == binary`, `config.drivers.last() == mergiraf`), not equality with the default.

problem: `merge_file_returns_the_merge_with_one_or_two_conflicts` passes only because this machine's ~/.gitconfig sets `merge.conflictstyle=zdiff3`. With no global config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null), git's merge style joins `A b c d E`/`X b c d Y` into one block and the `count == 2` assert fails. Any CI or fresh machine sees a red suite. The test dates from round 1.
fix:
Use a two-block input that splits under every conflict style, e.g. hunks separated by four or more alnum lines like `a
bb
cc
dd
ee
f
`, or set `merge.conflictStyle` in the conflict repo's config (`Setup::config`).

problem: `a_configured_merge_driver_with_markers_opens_from_disk_at_the_first_list` still passes if the `config.drivers.contains(name)` lookup is deleted: `mergiraf` then falls back to Text, git's text merge of OURS/THEIRS differs from the driver's `local`/`remote` block, so the file is Changed and gives `MarkersLeft{1}` + Disk view anyway. No test proves that a configured name gives Custom.

problem: #599 The capture-phase mousedown on scrollDOM also fires for presses on the scrollbar, so dragging a side's scrollbar retargets that side's mark to whatever change lies beside the thumb (or clears it to alone) although #54 rule 1 only speaks of clicks in the pane and on a change block; the next Enter then decides a different change than the one the user had outlined.

problem: #600 historyCommand matches only `event.key`, so on a non-Latin layout (Ctrl+Z gives key 'я' on Russian) undo works in the middle — CodeMirror falls back to the keyCode — but does nothing from a side pane or anywhere else, contradicting #54 'undoes anywhere in the shown file's window'.

problem: #601 After an icon click, a drag or a Ctrl/Cmd+click with the keyboard on a side, the outline moves on (settled) but the view never reveals it, so the outline can land off screen and the next Enter applies a change the user cannot see; #54 says a newly focused change off screen 'lands as WebStorm places a difference', while the brief's A5 says 'clicks never scroll' and the implementer chose no reveal.

problem: #602 #54 says 'waiting changes only beyond the screen in the pressed direction → nothing', which read literally means Down with changes only below the screen does nothing, while the brief, #587 and the patch (fromScreen has no lower bound; stepAlone returns null only when changes wait only above) jump down to the first one below; the verifier reading #54 as acceptance could fail correct behaviour.

problem: #603 decided() hands the keyboard over whenever the focused side has nothing waiting, even when the decision was on the other side and the focused side was already empty (e.g. ArrowLeft onto a finished local, then a click on a remote icon moves the keyboard to remote), which breaks #589's 'the keyboard stays where it was'.

problem: #604 A Ctrl/Cmd+click on a side that hits no waiting change is skipped by #pressed, but modClick does not consume it, so the browser focuses the side with its old mark still outlined instead of the side alone (rule 1).

problem: #605 Implementer-reported: WebKit moves DOM focus to DIV.cm-scroller when a side's scrollbar is pressed; the mark stays but the side loses cm-focused, so no outline and keys do not reach the side until the next click (browser behaviour, outside #599).

problem: #606 Implementer-reported: Ctrl/Cmd+click within POINT_HIT_PX of a zero-line change's bar is skipped by #pressed (changeAt hits it) but not consumed by modClick (openBlockAt needs len > 0), so the side gets focus with its old mark.

problem: #607 `decided()` calls `#reveal(focused)` whenever no handover happens, even when the decision left that side's mark unchanged. Plan §2 #54 moves the view only for 'a newly focused change', and #590 rejected re-placing a change that was not newly focused.
fix: Read the focused side's mark before `#dispatch` (for example, have SideFocus wrap the decision as `decide(run: () => void)` and take both the states snapshot and the marks itself, so #decide no longer reads the field for it). Call `#reveal` only when `markedId` of the focused side changed.

problem: #609 decided() reveals the focused side's mark after every decision, even when the decision did not move it. Example: keyboard on the left with change A outlined, the view wheel-scrolled down, then a click on the apply icon of another left change B (or Ctrl+click on B, a drag, or a remote icon). A still waits, so the mark stays on A and #reveal scrolls all panes back to A, away from the change the user just clicked. #54 reveals only a *newly focused* change, and the keyboard 'stays where it was'.
fix: Capture the focused side's mark before the dispatch (e.g. in #decide next to `before`, or have SideFocus snapshot `#mark(side)` for both sides) and call #reveal(focused) only when the settled mark differs from it.

problem: #610 Nothing at unit level covers the reveal-or-handover branch in decided() (#601). problem: #666 The two `#[serde(default)]` attributes make the generated `StoredSettings` `{ theme?: Theme; keys?: … }`, although Rust always sends both fields and nothing in Rust deserialises StoredSettings except the IPC `current` argument (the file is parsed field by field through `file::entry`). problem: #668 When the settings path is a dangling symlink (a dotfiles link whose target does not exist yet), `canonicalize` fails and the code falls back to the link path, and `load` reads it as missing. problem: #674 `link_target` resolves only one symlink hop. With `settings.json` → link B → existing dotfile C, the rename replaces link B with a regular file, so C silently stops getting changes. Round 1's `canonicalize` followed that chain, so this is a regression against rule 6 ('write to its resolved target so the link stays a link'), and the doc comment on `write_text` (line 98) overstates what the code does.
fix: Follow `read_link` in a loop while `symlink_metadata` says symlink, bounded by a named const (e.g. 40, Linux's MAXSYMLINKS) so a cycle cannot hang. Add a test `a_chain_of_settings_symlinks_stays_links_and_writes_the_last_target` (link → link → file: both stay links, and the file holds the change).

problem: #675 (same as previous) `link_target` follows only one link. When the settings link points to a second link (a dotfiles chain), the rename replaces that second link with a regular file. That breaks rule 6's 'write to its resolved target', a case round 1's `canonicalize` handled whenever the last file existed (implementer open risk 1, judged here as a regression).
fix: Keep calling `fs::read_link` while `symlink_metadata` reports a symlink. Join each relative target onto the current link's folder, and stop with an error after a named limit (e.g. `const MAX_LINK_HOPS: usize = 40`, Linux's MAXSYMLINKS) so a cycle cannot loop forever. Add a test with a link → link → file chain that checks both links are still links.

problem: #676 `entries()` always writes `theme`, so a `set_keys` on a hand-written file without a `theme` entry now adds `"theme": "dark"`. Round 1 left that entry out, and architecture §3.6 and brief rule 5 say a change replaces only one entry. The value means the same, but the file gains a line.

problem: #677 `link_target` returns `path` itself when `path` is not a link, so the name promises a link's target and the doc comment has to correct it.

problem: #678 `for _ in 0..MAX_LINK_HOPS` follows at most 40 links and never checks the 40th target. A chain of exactly 40 links, which Linux reads fine, fails to write with the message "more than 40 symlinks in a row". That contradicts the error text, the const's comment ('more links in a row than this') and MAXSYMLINKS, and the same file is readable but not writable.
fix: Loop `for _ in 0..=MAX_LINK_HOPS` so that 40 links are followed and the 41st is refused, which matches both the message and Linux's limit.

problem: #679 (same as previous) `for _ in 0..MAX_LINK_HOPS` follows at most 39 links before it must reach a non-link. A chain of exactly 40 links, which the kernel and so `load` accept, fails the write with "more than 40 symlinks in a row". This contradicts both the error text and the doc on `MAX_LINK_HOPS` ("more links in a row than this is a cycle").
fix: Iterate `0..=MAX_LINK_HOPS`, so 40 links resolve and the 41st errors, matching Linux's MAXSYMLINKS.

problem: #754 focus.ts writes the state file itself (lines 36 and 51) and makes its own spawn-then-record step (`launch` + `writeState` with the proc appended). It also recomputes the logs folder as `join(app.folder, "logs")` (line 33), next to start.ts:41. The rule "every spawned process is recorded in the state file at once" and the logs location now have two copies, so the state file has two write paths.
